Comfort Upgrades That Transform Touring

Factory standard motorcycles are designed for average riders doing average distances. If you are touring 300 miles a day for a week, those factory settings quickly reveal their limitations. A few well-chosen comfort upgrades can transform a tolerable touring experience into a genuinely enjoyable one, letting you arrive at each destination fresher and happier.

Heated Grips

Heated grips are the number one comfort upgrade for UK touring. They warm your palms from below, complementing insulated gloves that warm from above. The combination means comfortable hands in all but the most extreme cold. Most heated grip kits cost under one hundred pounds and can be fitted at home in about an hour.

Oxford HotGrips Premium — The best-selling aftermarket grips with five heat settings and an intelligent controller that prevents battery drain. Available for touring and sport handlebars.

OEM heated grips — Most manufacturers offer heated grips as accessories. They integrate seamlessly with the handlebar controls and look factory-fitted.

Seat Upgrades

A standard motorcycle seat becomes uncomfortable after 90 minutes for most riders. Upgrading the seat is the second most impactful comfort improvement:

  • Gel seat pads — Affordable gel pads that sit on top of your existing seat. Products like AirHawk and Wild Ass cushions use air cells to distribute pressure and reduce numbness.
  • Custom seats — Companies like Corbin, Sargent, and Bagster make custom touring seats with better foam density, wider bases, and improved pillion comfort. Expensive but transformative.
  • Heated seats — Some aftermarket seats include heating elements. A warm seat on a cold morning is pure luxury.
  • Sheepskin covers — A natural sheepskin seat cover improves comfort surprisingly well by distributing pressure and wicking moisture.

Bar Risers and Handlebar Adjustments

If you suffer wrist, shoulder, or back pain on tour, the handlebar position may be wrong for your body. Bar risers lift the handlebars by 20-30mm, shifting weight off your wrists and onto the seat. Adjustable bar mounts let you move the handlebars forward or backward for a custom fit. These modifications cost under fifty pounds and can be transformative.

Footpeg Lowering and Highway Pegs

Lowering kits for footpegs reduce the knee bend angle for taller riders, reducing knee and hip fatigue. Highway pegs mounted on the crash bars give you an alternative foot position for motorway cruising, allowing you to stretch your legs without stopping.

Comfort is not a luxury — it is a safety feature. A rider in pain or discomfort has slower reactions, poorer concentration, and makes worse decisions. Investing in comfort upgrades directly improves your touring safety.

faq.q: How can I improve seat comfort cheaply?
faq.a: A gel seat pad from AirHawk or Wild Ass sits on your existing seat and uses air cells to distribute pressure and reduce numbness, and a natural sheepskin cover works surprisingly well by spreading pressure and wicking moisture. Both cost far less than a custom seat from Corbin, Sargent or Bagster.

faq.q: Will bar risers help wrist and back pain?
faq.a: If you suffer wrist, shoulder or back pain on tour, the handlebar position may be wrong for your body. Bar risers lift the bars by 20-30mm, shifting weight off your wrists onto the seat, and adjustable mounts let you move the bars for a custom fit, all for under fifty pounds.

faq.q: Is comfort really a safety issue?
faq.a: Yes. Comfort is not a luxury but a safety feature, because a rider in pain or discomfort has slower reactions, poorer concentration and makes worse decisions. Investing in heated grips, a better seat and the right bar position directly improves your touring safety over long days.
